turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come through when you're ready. Sorry you've waited, my little boy's off nursery with a cough and the whole morning's slipped.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, no worries.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, err, give me a second, it's making me sign in again. Right. What can I do for you?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I've come because I'm so tired. And I get breathless going up the stairs.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Breathless on the stairs. Sorry, say that once more, I was clicking the wrong tab.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Umm, one flight at the flat and I'm puffing. I'm only 23.
[SEG0007] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, she's been like this three months, proper exhausted. And her periods are really heavy, that's why I dragged her in.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are your periods actually heavy?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, mum, they're normal, same as always. And it's not three months, more like six weeks. I don't know, doctor, I can't pin the day it started.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): The screen just refreshed. Six weeks, did you say, or three months?
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three months. It was after her birthday in March, I remember.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know. Six weeks feels closer, but the actual date, I don't know.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll leave it as somewhere between six weeks and three months. Any chest pain with the breathlessness?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough? Wheeze at night or anything?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, no cough. I don't wheeze.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Weight's the same.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bowels, passing water, any trouble there?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No, all fine. Um. Nothing like that.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): It says vegetarian on the triage note. Is that still right? Sorry, read it to me, the box is tiny.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, strict vegetarian. No meat, no fish, since I was sixteen. I do eat properly.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She lives on toast, doctor, I'm not joking.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not fair. I have three meals. Lentils, eggs, veg. I'm just vegetarian.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the ice. Who put ice on the form?
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): She told me outside she crunches ice all the time. My sister did the same all through her pregnancy, we had to keep the freezer stocked.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah that's me. I crunch ice constantly, last few weeks. I don't know why, doctor.

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): So what's going on in the body, if the iron's low you haven't enough haemoglobin to carry the oxygen, the muscles and the brain run short, and that's the tiredness and the puffing on stairs, and the ice craving is the body looking for iron. It's a mechanism, not a second illness.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): I was going to skip the tests and just give you ferrous sulphaite, 200 milligrams once a day.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Tablets? Umm, I don't know, doctor, I'm rubbish with tablets.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She is. She forgets the vitamin ones I buy her.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Actually, no, ignore that. Working impression, this is probably iron deficiency, from the tiredness, the stairs, the ice and the vegetarian diet, but I can't confirm it today. Bloods first, the nurse will take them today, full blood count, ferritin, B12 and folate. We start iron only if the ferritin's low.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me look at you. Chin up a bit.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Conjunctivae are pale. Tongue's fine. No ankle swelling. Chest is clear, I can't hear a wheeze.
[SEG0035] person_1 (NURSE): Obs are done. Blood pressure 118 over 74, pulse 92, oxygen sats 99 percent.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pulse again? This fan is ridiculous.
[SEG0037] person_1 (NURSE): Pulse 92. Sats still 99. 118 over 74.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ta. Anyone in the family had anaemia?
[SEG0039] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I did, after she was born. Iron tablets for months. Nothing on her dad's side that I know of.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): While we wait on the bloods, have vitamin C with your meals, a bit of pepper or orange juice, keep the lentils and the greens, and don't drink tea alongside your food, it grabs the iron. Reception will book you back with me in two weeks for the results.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Right. I'll try and remember the food bit. I don't know if I will, doctor.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Recorded symptom of heavy periods as present/disputed is wrong: the patient denied heavy periods and said they are normal/same as always; only the mother suggested heavy periods.
Doctor initially proposed ferrous sulphate 200 mg once daily, then explicitly withdrew that plan and said to ignore it pending blood tests.
Chest examination finding omitted: chest was clear.
Follow-up detail omitted: reception will book the patient back with the same doctor in two weeks for the blood test results.
